messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Ventus7b service degradation — elevated 5xx/timeouts (status + next steps)

Hi Santiago / Elena,

I wanted to reach out right away with an operational note: we are observing an elevated rate of 5xx errors and sporadic timeouts from the Ventus7b model when handling certain multimodal prompt patterns. Impact: a subset of requests from Aqua Partners (your production routing binding) have been returning 503s or timing out in the last 45 minutes.

What we know so far:
- Start: ~07:25 PDT; spike peaked ~07:48 PDT.
- Symptoms: transient 503 responses, some requests hitting the platform timeout at 12s.
- Scope: ~3.6% of production tokens from your routing to Ventus7b; other models unaffected.

Immediate mitigation in progress:
- Automated fallback to Ventus7b-quantized-compat (lower latency variant) has been enabled for your account.
- Rate limiting thresholds temporarily reduced for burst traffic to stabilize the serving pool.

Short-term ask from you: please monitor your error dashboards for any remaining 503s and forward any recent sample request IDs you want prioritized for log pulls.

We will keep you updated as we gather root-cause data and finalize a recovery plan. Our engineering lead (Ben Carter) is on the incident and will follow up with technical detail. Sorry for the disruption — we know this impacts your user flows and will prioritize.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ventus7b-sample-5xx-snippet.txt (sample stack traces), ventus7b-metrics-window-1012.csv (minute-level error rates)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ventus7b service degradation — initial triage notes

Markus / team,

Quick triage summary from runtime ops:
- Error signature matches an unexpected KV cache eviction pattern under mixed-length prefixes. When the model hits a specific cache churn threshold, one of the attention kernel fallbacks throws a transient 503 at the serving layer.
- We have a reproducible load test that triggers the fault (local staging).
- Mitigations applied: lowered batch size cap and enabled circuit breaker for affected nodes; fallback path to quantized variant is active for customer traffic.

Next steps we are executing now:
1) Collect expanded logs for the window 07:20–08:10 PDT and push to shared Drive (done).
2) Push a hotfix to the serving runtime that increases KV cache retention for Ventus7b (ETA: 3–4 hours).
3) Run canary traffic on a small subset of nodes, then lift the temporary rate caps.

I will coordinate the hotfix rollout with Karthik on kernel selection change and we should have a more stable signal by early afternoon.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi Santiago / Elena,

Quick update following Irene's triage: we have identified a cache-eviction-triggered failure mode in the Ventus7b serving runtime. Engineering has prepared a targeted hotfix that increases KV retention and adjusts attention kernel selection for the workload patterns that surfaced the issue.

What we will do next for Aqua Partners:
- 12:15 PDT: route a small percentage (~1%) of your traffic to canary nodes running the hotfix.
- 12:40 PDT: expand to 10% if canary is healthy.
- 13:10 PDT: full rollout and then lift temporary rate caps.

We will monitor your request IDs and error rates during each step and only proceed with expansion if 503/timout rates drop to baseline. Ben will send a separate note with real-time metrics.

If you would like us to hold additional traffic (or prefer waiting for post-rollout confirmation before resuming any queued requests) let us know and we will adapt.

Thanks for bearing with us.

Best,
Markus

Subject: Ventus7b post-incident summary & next steps (action items)

Santiago / Elena — follow-up with final items from our internal post-incident review. Thanks again for the patience and the request ID; that helped us validate the root cause.

Incident recap (concise):
- Window: 2026-10-12 07:25–08:10 PDT.
- Root cause: a KV cache eviction threshold combined with an attention-kernel fallback that produced transient 503s under mixed-length prefixes in Ventus7b.
- Impact: ~3.6% of your Ventus7b requests returned 503 or timed out; no data was exposed beyond request metadata.

Actions completed:
- Hotfix deployed to serving runtime (increased KV retention, kernel selection change) — rolled to all production nodes for Ventus7b by 14:10 PDT on 10/12.
- Canary verification and staged rollout completed; error rate returned to baseline within the rollout window.
- Temporary rate caps lifted once stability confirmed.

Committed follow-ups (items we will deliver by dates):
1) Postmortem document with technical appendix and mitigations — 2026-10-15 (attached draft: postmortem-draft-ventus7b.docx).
2) A kerneled regression test added to our model onboarding suite to catch similar cache-fallback patterns — 2026-10-20.
3) Option for Aqua Partners to pin to a Ventus7b variant with higher KV retention for an SLA-backed routing (if desired) — change order available on request.

If you want a short sync to walk through the postmortem and the mitigation plan I can set up 30 minutes tomorrow. Otherwise I'll share the final postmortem and the logs we pulled for req_20261012_0729_AY5W.

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll follow up with the final doc and a test plan.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
